title: thatteOS: a microkernel operating system written in ManiT, a balanced-ternary language
description:
thatteOS is a microkernel operating system written entirely in ManiT, a systems language whose native number system is balanced ternary. It builds and runs on Linux today in hosted mode, by way of the maniTC compiler's LLVM backend.

Designing an operating system around a three-valued machine word changes its structure rather than its surface. Privilege is one trit deep, so three rings fall out of the number system itself. Virtual memory uses trit-trie page tables, a radix-3 walk in place of the usual radix-512. The kernel schedules a photonic-ternary computing fabric in the way a conventional kernel schedules a processor, with capability security built on the schedule.

Includes a scheduler, message-passing IPC, trit-stream channels, a TTY driver, an interactive shell, and a small userspace.

Distributed under AGPL-3.0-or-later with a syscall-boundary note: user programs invoking thatteOS system calls are not derivative works. A commercial licence is available.
